name: Namaste
verifiedMeaning: Traditional Indian greeting, expressing honor, welcome, and peaceful respect ('I bow to you').
instructions: Bring both palms together at chest level in front of the sternum.
Keep fingers pointing straight upwards and slightly angled forward.
Gently bow head slightly while maintaining hand contact.
keyLandmarks: Dual-hand palm juxtaposition at wrist; finger tips aligned (landmarks 4, 8, 12, 16, 20 parallel).
attribution: ISLRTC (Indian Sign Language Research and Training Centre) Standard Vocabulary

name: Thank You
verifiedMeaning: Expression of gratitude and appreciation towards the conversational partner.
instructions: Touch the fingertips of your flat dominant hand lightly to your chin or lower lip.
Extend your hand smoothly outward and forward toward the person you are thanking.
Accompany with a pleasant facial expression.
keyLandmarks: Dominant hand flat palm (fingers extended); trajectory from chin position forward toward camera.
attribution: ISLRTC Standard Vocabulary & Deaf Enabled Foundation Lexicon

name: Please
verifiedMeaning: Polite request token used when asking for assistance, permission, or consideration.
instructions: Place your open flat dominant hand over your chest area.
Move hand in gentle clockwise circular motion while maintaining light contact or hovering close.
Keep fingers naturally together and palm flat against torso plane.
keyLandmarks: Open flat palm centered on chest; circular spatial trajectory in frontal XY plane.
attribution: ISLRTC Lexicon / National Institute for Speech and Hearing

name: Help
verifiedMeaning: Urgent or general request for assistance, aid, or physical support.
instructions: Extend non-dominant hand palm-up horizontally as a flat base.
Form a closed fist with dominant hand with thumb pointing slightly up ('A' shape).
Place dominant fist onto the flat palm and raise both hands together slightly.
keyLandmarks: Base palm flat horizontal (wrist to tip horizontal); dominant closed fist atop palm lifting vertically.
attribution: ISLRTC Vocabulary Reference & All India Federation of the Deaf

name: Yes
instructions: Make a closed fist with your dominant hand held at chest-shoulder height.
Bend your wrist gently forward and downward, mimicking the motion of a nodding head.
Repeat the nodding motion once smoothly.
keyLandmarks: Closed fist (landmarks 8, 12, 16, 20 curled into palm); periodic wrist pitch oscillation.

name: No
verifiedMeaning: Negative response, denial, disagreement, or refusal.
instructions: Extend your index finger and middle finger while keeping ring and pinky closed.
Quickly snap the extended fingers down against the thumb in a pinching motion.
Optionally shake dominant index finger from side to side with slight head shake.
keyLandmarks: Index and middle extended (distal joints straight) snapping into opposition with thumb tip (landmark 4).

name: Water
verifiedMeaning: Request for drinking water or reference to liquid hydration.
instructions: Form a 'W' shape with dominant hand (index, middle, ring fingers spread upright, thumb holding pinky).
Tap the side of index finger against the chin or near lips twice.
Hold forearm upright and steady.
keyLandmarks: Three middle fingers upright (landmarks 8, 12, 16 extended); thumb crossed over pinky; chin proximity.

name: Food / Eat
verifiedMeaning: Reference to meals, hunger, eating, or nourishment.
instructions: Bring all fingertips of dominant hand together into a tapered bunch touching thumb ('O' handshape).
Tap the bunched fingertips toward lips or mouth twice.
Keep wrist relaxed and movement natural.
keyLandmarks: All fingertips clustered (landmarks 4, 8, 12, 16, 20 distance < 0.15 normalized); position near lower face.

name: Good
verifiedMeaning: Positive appraisal, well-being, high quality, or satisfaction.
instructions: Make a firm fist with dominant thumb pointing straight up in a classic thumbs-up posture.
Hold upright at chest height with confident posture.
Maintain stable position with slight forward emphasis.
keyLandmarks: Thumb tip extended vertically (y_thumb < y_wrist - 0.4); fingers 8, 12, 16, 20 fully curled into palm.

name: Bad
verifiedMeaning: Negative appraisal, dissatisfaction, poor condition, or disapproval.
instructions: Start with dominant hand in thumbs-up or flat palm at chest level.
Quickly rotate wrist downward to point thumb down or flick fingers downward toward floor.
Accompany with subtle negative facial expression.
keyLandmarks: Thumb inverted pointing downwards (y_thumb > y_wrist + 0.2); downward forearm trajectory.

name: Friend
verifiedMeaning: Companionship, peer relationship, mutual trust, or camaraderie.
instructions: Curve both index fingers into small hooks while keeping other fingers loosely curled.
Interlock the two curved index fingers together in front of chest.
Reverse and interlock them the other way smoothly.
keyLandmarks: Dual-hand hook posture; index finger tips (8_left, 8_right) interlocking with Euclidean proximity < 0.1.

name: Doctor / Medicine
verifiedMeaning: Medical professional, clinical treatment, prescription, or healthcare facility.
instructions: Hold non-dominant arm forward with wrist facing upward in resting posture.
Extend dominant index and middle fingers together (two fingers straight).
Tap the two fingertips gently onto the pulse area of the non-dominant wrist twice.
keyLandmarks: Non-dominant wrist resting horizontal; dominant index & middle tips contacting wrist area (radial pulse).

name: Emergency
verifiedMeaning: Urgent critical situation requiring immediate intervention or safety measures.
instructions: Raise dominant hand with open fingers spread wide above chest height.
Shake or wave hand rapidly side-to-side with urgency.
Alternatively tap chest rapidly with firm open hand.
keyLandmarks: Open hand with maximum finger spread (inter-fingertip distance > 0.4); high-frequency lateral oscillation.

name: Stop
verifiedMeaning: Direct instruction to cease action, halt, pause, or wait.
instructions: Hold dominant hand vertically upright in front of you with palm facing flat toward the other person.
Keep all five fingers straight and together.
Deliver hand forward with a firm, decisive stopping motion.
keyLandmarks: Open vertical palm (wrist to middle tip vertical); palm facing directly towards camera (z coordinates uniform).
